cards.text: Friend, Amos was one of the sheepherders of Tekoa (Amos 1:1), and he's been bringing Israel some HEAVY news. God says He'll destroy the sinful kingdom and shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve. But He also says He will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob.
Then the LORD looks ahead to 'that day,' and He talks about the tent of David. And friend, that tent is DOWN: gaps, ruins, the works.

cards.question: The tent of David has fallen, full of gaps and ruins. What does the LORD promise to do with it?

answers.text: Rebuild it like it was long ago
Leave it in ruins as a warning
Tear down what is left of it

cards.text: Repair the gaps, restore the ruins, rebuild the whole thing. That's not a touch-up, friend, that's the WHOLE renovation show, demo day to the big reveal.

cards.question: Once the tent of David is rebuilt, what does the LORD say they will possess?

answers.text: Edom's remnant and the nations bearing His name
Philistia's cities and the whole land of Moab
Egypt's fields and the faraway land of Cush

cards.question: The LORD says someone else will have to do the work of rebuilding the tent of David.

cards.text: He signs it right there: "declares the LORD, who will do this." Friend, that's the one contractor who never says 'I'll be back Tuesday' and then disappears for three weeks.
Then the LORD says, "Behold, the days are coming," and paints a picture of the farms. Get this: the plowman will overtake the reaper.

cards.question: The plowman catches up to the reaper before the harvest is done. What does that tell you about the harvest?

answers.text: It's so big it never seems to end
It's so small it's over too fast
It's spoiled before anyone gathers it

cards.text: Same with the treader of grapes catching up to the sower of seed. That's me still pulling one batch out of the oven while the NEXT batch of dough is tapping me on the shoulder like, 'Papa. Papa. PAPA. We're READY.'

cards.question: With grapes coming in like that, the mountains will drip with sweet ___, and all the hills will flow with it.
Looking ahead to those days, the LORD says He will restore His people Israel from ___.
The LORD talks about the ruined cities. What will His people do with them?

answers.text: Rebuild them and live in them

cards.text: Then the LORD gets to the vineyards. Earlier in Amos, God warned Israel they wouldn't drink the wine from the vineyards they planted (Amos 5:11).

cards.question: This time, the LORD says His people will plant vineyards and drink their wine.

cards.text: Same with the gardens: they make them, and they eat their fruit. That's finishing the big project at work and actually getting the credit, with no coworker jumping in at the meeting like, 'Sooo, I had this idea…'
Then the LORD turns the planting picture onto His people themselves. He says He will firmly plant them in their own land.

cards.question: Firmly planted, the LORD says His people will never again be ___ from their land.
The LORD says the land Israel is planted in is land they won for themselves.

cards.text: It closes with "says the LORD your God," the last words of the whole book of Amos. After all those hard warnings, the final word is a PROMISE, friend, and I'm over here crying into my apron like it's the end of a movie.
